records.completion_scope: All selected material geographic components and the actual terminal were read on original cartography at ordinary corridor scale. The three distinct map sheets join across the provincial/territorial boundary and the adjacent map-sheet edge. No missing material source or connector remains at that scale. This is neither exact bank/vertex matching nor geometry revalidation.
records.region: Northern Manitoba and Nunavut, Canada; western lake chain, cross-boundary connector, Geillini Lake/River and Hudson Bay coast.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Primary map pixels cover the selected headward lake-and-stream chain in northern Manitoba, the short connection across the Nunavut boundary, the southern Geillini Lake approach and outlet, and the Geillini River corridor to Hudson Bay. The downstream label supports Geillini River as a representative system candidate. It does not name every western feeder, lake passage or connector.
records.supported_name_scope: Geillini River is the mapped downstream representative identity; the western unnamed feeder/lake-chain components and Geillini Lake remain separately scoped.

component_scope_limits: Geillini River is the mapped downstream river label, retained only as a representative candidate.
Geillini Lake is a distinct lake name. The upstream Manitoba lake complex includes separately labeled Falloon and Nabel lakes; these labels are not replaced by the downstream river name.

Names for individually unnamed headward ponds, connecting streams and smaller intervening lakes remain null. Nearby Savage, Dutchak and Schwartz lake labels serve as geographic orientation and are not all asserted as selected lake passages.

Historical NLUIS cartography also shows brown local-place labels. Their precise modern spelling, alias status and geographic naming scope were not independently established and are not promoted to candidate aliases.
The 1979 NLUIS maps and 2002 provincial compilation establish historical cartographic correspondence, not present registry status or a uniform whole-feature scalar name.

records.region: Guatemala; Concepción–Chilascó–Sinanjá–Panimá–Matanzas–Polochic main feeder, Cahabón branch, Lago de Izabal and Río Dulce to Livingston.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The main selected route follows the Concepción–Chilascó–Sinanjá–Panimá–Matanzas feeder into Polochic, then Lago de Izabal, Río Dulce and El Golfete to Caribbean waters at Livingston. Two separate selected fragments follow the Cahabón corridor into Polochic. Original mapping covers all five fragments and their junction/lake/terminal settings.
records.completion_scope: Original CONRED sheets plus three overlapping source-native GeoVisit corridor views cover every selected component, headward setting, major confluence, lake passage and terminal. Bounded SEGEPLAN prose supplies source-described transitions and integrated identity. Optional stopped publications do not leave an unseen geographic connector.
records.supported_name_scope: The representative is SEGEPLAN’s integrated Lago de Izabal–Río Dulce hydrographic system. It does not make Concepción, Chilascó, Sinanjá, Panimá, Matanzas, Polochic and Cahabón alternate names for one uniform river. The complete scalar and Korean name remain null.

records.region: Southeastern Santiago del Estero and northeastern Córdoba, Argentina; Malbrán–Palo Negro plains/wetlands and the eastern Laguna Mar Chiquita basin.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: Full original-map coverage shows a composite of plain/interfluve ground, marshes, individual lakes and a long lake-interior passage. No representative natural-watercourse name is established for that complete terrestrial/wetland/lake route.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The complete selected Malbrán–Palo Negro–eastern Mar Chiquita corridor is geographically covered by original IGN cartography. The route mixes plain/interfluve ground, extensive marshes, the Laguna El Mojón Colorado setting, unnamed wet depressions and a long passage inside Laguna Mar Chiquita. Its actual endpoint lies inside the southeastern lake basin, northwest of La Paquita. No representative watercourse hydronym is established for this whole selected path; this is a completed naming-scope hold, with no missing material connector.
records.completion_scope: A complete original 1:500,000 overview and three overlapping original 1:250,000 panels were acquired normally and read in unmarked form and with a separate private selected-route orientation. They cover the initial plain, major bends, road/rail crossing, lake and wetland passages, intervening ground and actual terminal. A normally acquired 2006 primary scientific chapter supplies independent regional geomorphology and observed historical lake-extent context, including its original Figure 4. Differences between mapped inundation extents are preserved rather than treated as missing map coverage. This is ordinary geographic/source correspondence, not a validation of model hydraulics or precise banks.

naming_scope_details.terminal_receiving_lake: Laguna Mar Chiquita / Mar de Ansenuza
naming_scope_details.actual_terminal: Inside the southeastern lake basin, northwest of La Paquita
component_scope_limits: No single river name is established for the complete selected line. Mapped non-channel plain and wetland geography does not itself become a named watercourse.
Laguna El Mojón Colorado names a particular lake/wetland setting traversed near Palo Negro; it is not a representative name for the entire system.
Laguna Beltrán and Laguna de los Porongos are nearby named lakes that the selected line passes to the west and east, respectively. Their labels are not transferred to other unnamed depressions.

Laguna Mar Chiquita, also labeled Mar de Ansenuza on the 1:500,000 overview, is the mapped receiving lake and terminal setting. Its name does not identify the terrestrial/wetland northern route as a river.

The 2006 chapter distinguishes the eastern lagoon–wetland chain associated with an ancient Salado connection from the central Dulce course and the western Saladillos system. Historical regional association does not establish a present selected connection to Río Salado or justify naming the selected line Río Dulce or Río Saladillo.

The historical 1:250,000 mosaic depicts a substantially larger connected northern lake-water area than the febrero 2026 overview. Neither source establishes present shoreline, permanent inundation, flow direction through every wet hollow, a dated transition between the mapped states, or a uniform scalar river identity.

The retained selection has one mainstem FID and no separately selected tributary/reservoir feature. Formal name-registry status is unverified; accepted, scalar and Korean names remain null and application remains false.

completion_scope.selected_lake_or_reservoir_passage: La Paloma eastward river approach, reservoir/junction setting and northwest outlet continuation are supported jointly by original hydrographic and land-cover views and DGA prose. Cogotí and Recoleta are neighboring feeder-system reservoirs, not selected passages.
completion_scope.headward_mismatch_vs_gap: The independent field-study elevation map shows the distinctive eastern international-boundary bulge and natural interior Gordito valley. Combined with the MMA linework, the selected boundary excursion and the return across the Gordito drainage/upland setting are geographically readable as a noncontinuous-river connector. This affirmative terrain/boundary correspondence, rather than mere absence of a line, closes the former headward material gap.
completion_scope.scale_limit: Generalized component/corridor correspondence only. No exact bank, vertex, boundary demarcation, current wetness or flow-direction survey is asserted.

records.region: Coquimbo, Chile; Gordito/boundary-upland head setting, Grande–La Paloma–Hurtado junction and Limarí Pacific outlet.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The independently inspected terrain/border map establishes the eastern headward excursion and return as a boundary/upland connector distinct from the natural Gordito–Las Cuevas–Grande channel. The downstream Grande–La Paloma–Limarí identity cannot name that whole composite selection.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The complete selected setting is accounted for at ordinary corridor scale. The short head lies in the Gordito tributary setting, but the following eastern excursion occupies the mapped international-border/upland band and then cuts back across the Gordito drainage toward Grande. The natural downstream corridor continues through La Paloma reservoir, lower Grande and the Hurtado junction into Limarí and its Pacific estuary. Because the head connector is not the mapped continuous river route, no whole-object representative identity is assigned. This is a completed geographic review with naming scope held, not an unread-source/connector hold.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
